I am an old man, I never went to school, I farm the way my father showed me. This plot here is 1.35 hectares, I grow mixed things on it — I put different crops together so if one fails another one feeds us. Living here near Dar es Salaam, the soil is sandy and tired, but I cannot buy the fertilizer bags — one bag costs too much money and I do not trust to put my shillings there when the rain can cheat me. I will put the cow manure and kitchen ash I have at home, that one is free, and I use the seeds I saved from last harvest like always. My sons and my wife help me, and when the weeding time comes heavy I will call two, three people from the neighbourhood for a few days to help me finish.
